evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3464869 is a 599.94 USD online product-R purchase in billing region 327.0 on 2016-11-17 14:03:36. Card C03042-K1 is a mastercard credit owned by C03042.
Region 327.0 has 0 prior purchases on this card before the alert.
Closed cases on this card: CC-0615 (confirmed_fraud, card_not_present_new_device); CC-1313 (cleared, none); CC-3886 (confirmed_fraud, card_not_present_new_device).
Device Trident/7.0 | Windows 8.1 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1680x1050 made this purchase; shared_cards_on_device found no other payment cards on this profile.
Email domain anonymous.com is present on the flagged purchase; email_fanout found 22 other cards, treated as too common for R6.
Billing region 327.0 appears on 7 other cards in the local 1-hop fan-out. Region sharing is recorded, not treated as proof of a shared origin.
Supports fraud: new device, mixed-channel takeover, or a tight shared-origin cluster is present on the neighborhood.
Episode reconstruction grouped 3 transactions around 3464869 using history, device, amount outliers, and NEXT edges 3462404, 3468946.
Customer denied the purchase and still has the card.

R2 Customer denies: When the customer denies the transaction, recommend BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE. Add FILE_REPORT when exposure exceeds 1000 USD, a shared device is present, or another card's fraud is connected.
Account takeover: Mixed-channel behavior inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies. Stolen credentials, not only a stolen card number.

Closed case CC-0255: Case CC-0255: cardholder C02354 reported unrecognized activity on card C02354-K2. 7 transaction(s) between 2016-07-06 and 2016-07-08 totaling $1,167.08 were confirmed fraudulent. Mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder; credentials and card data both used. Online transactions came from a iOS Device on mobile safari 10.0. Card blocked and reissued. Customer reimbursed.

FFIEC authentication guidance: FFIEC guidance expects layered authentication. A new device or credential change on an online purchase is a reason to step up authentication, not automatic proof of fraud.

sar.narrative: On 2016-11-16, card C03042-K1 belonging to customer C03042 was used for a 599.94 USD online transaction 3464869 in billing region 327.0, country 87.0. The product code was R. Episode reconstruction identified 3 related transaction(s) totaling 1461.99 USD from 2016-11-16 to 2016-11-18. Graph neighborhood review found this activity inconsistent with the cardholder's established pattern or linked it to a shared origin, email cluster, or mixed-channel takeover. Online purchase 3464869 used a device not seen on this card, shortly after in-person activity. That mixed-channel shift is treated as stolen credentials rather than a stolen card number alone. The investigation treated the purchase as unauthorized. Connected cards recommended for monitoring: none beyond the flagged card. The flagged card is recommended for restriction pending reissue. Total unauthorized amount: 1461.99 USD. This report is filed so a regulator can review the episode on its own.
